plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 41: Atomic Structure
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.

elements: vertical z axis with upward arrowhead, labeled 'z' at top
horizontal unlabeled axis crossing the z axis at the origin, extending mostly to the right
origin point at the left-center of the frame where all vectors start
seven identical-length olive-green arrows fanning from the origin into the right half-plane (m = +3 .. -3)
dashed circular arc through all seven arrow tips, showing common magnitude |L| = sqrt(l(l+1))ħ
label 'L' with vector arrow above the topmost (m = +3) arrow tip
dashed horizontal projection lines from each arrow tip back to the z axis
tick marks on the z axis at 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, 0, -ħ, -2ħ, -3ħ
tick labels: 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ (above origin) and -ħ, -2ħ, -3ħ (below origin)
four thin angle arcs of increasing radius from the +z axis to the four upper arrows
angle labels θ0 (innermost, opening to the horizontal m=0 arrow), θ1, θ2, θ3 (outermost, closing on the steepest m=+3 arrow)
faint continuous fan of grey vectors (hidden by default) representing classically allowed arbitrary orientations

interactions.label: Allowed m value
interactions.teaches: Stepping m from -l to +l shows the tip sliding to the next ħ tick while the arrow length never changes — Lz is quantized in units of ħ, the magnitude is fixed.

interactions.label: Orientations
interactions.teaches: Comparing the seven allowed vectors with a dense grey fan makes visible that quantum mechanics forbids all but a discrete set of polar angles.

interactions.label: Orbital quantum number l
interactions.teaches: Raising l lengthens every vector to sqrt(l(l+1))ħ and adds two more allowed projections, so the number of states 2l+1 and the magnitude grow together while the arrow tips never reach ±|L| on the z axis.
Hovering a vector reveals its m value, Lz = mħ, and polar angle cosθ = m/sqrt(l(l+1)), tying the picture to the formula.

demo_steps.title: The full fan
demo_steps.narration: Seven equal-length vectors fan out from the origin, their tips on a dashed arc of radius sqrt(12)ħ. Dashed lines show their z components stepping in equal units of ħ.

demo_steps.title: Maximum projection, m = +3
demo_steps.narration: Only the m = +3 vector remains: its projection lands on 3ħ, yet the arrow reaches beyond that on the arc — the vector can never lie fully along z.

demo_steps.title: Stepping down to m = 0
demo_steps.narration: Rotating to m = 0 lays the vector along the horizontal axis; the angle θ0 from the z axis is 90°, and the length is unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Negative projection, m = -2
demo_steps.narration: Below the axis the same ħ steps repeat: the tip's dashed line meets -2ħ, so Lz can be negative while |L| stays sqrt(12)ħ.

demo_steps.title: What classical physics would allow
demo_steps.narration: The faint grey fan shows every orientation a classical vector could take. Quantum mechanics keeps only the seven highlighted directions.

demo_steps.title: Change l
demo_steps.narration: At l = 2 the arc shrinks to sqrt(6)ħ and only five orientations survive; magnitude and the count of allowed Lz values move together.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D diagram in the xz-plane, viewed front-on (no depth). Scale: 1ħ = 1 world unit. Origin sits at screen-left-center, about 20% in from the left edge and vertically centered. z axis runs vertically from z = -4.2 to z = +4.6 with an arrowhead on top and the italic label 'z' beside the tip; horizontal axis runs from x = -1.2 to x = +4.4 with no label. Vector length R = sqrt(l(l+1))ħ (l=3 → 3.464; l=2 → 2.449; l=1 → 1.414; l=0 → 0). Each allowed vector points at polar angle θ_m from +z with cosθ_m = m/sqrt(l(l+1)); for l=3 these are 30.0°, 54.7°, 73.2°, 90°, 106.8°, 125.3°, 150.0°, all in the +x half-plane. Dashed circular arc of radius R spans from θ = 150° up through 30° (i.e. the right half-arc, from just below the lowest tip to just above the highest). Dashed horizontal projection lines run from each tip leftwards to the z axis at heights z = mħ = 3,2,1,0,-1,-2,-3; short tick marks and labels 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, -ħ, -2ħ, -3ħ placed to the LEFT of the z axis (origin unlabeled). Four angle arcs centered on origin, all starting on the +z axis and sweeping clockwise to their vector: θ0 radius 0.7 sweeping 0→90°, θ1 radius 1.1 sweeping 0→73.2°, θ2 radius 1.6 sweeping 0→54.7°, θ3 radius 2.2 sweeping 0→30°; each label sits just outside its arc midpoint in the wedge between the z axis and the vector, stacked upward in the order θ0 (lowest) to θ3 (highest). Label 'L' with an overhead vector arrow sits just outside the arc near the m=+3 tip, upper-right. Colors: vectors and arrowheads olive green #84A625 (line width ~3px, solid triangular heads); axes, arc, projection lines, angle arcs, tick labels all black/dark grey #1A1A1A, with the arc and projection lines dashed (~6px dash, 4px gap); classical-continuum fan drawn in grey #BBBBBB at 35% opacity with ~60 evenly spaced thin rays over 0–180°.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera looking down -Z at the xz-plane (pure 2D). Build arrows from THREE.Line/shaft + ConeGeometry or a Line2 with a small triangle mesh head so head size stays constant. Dashed elements via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Labels (z, 3ħ…-3ħ, θ0–θ3, vector L) as CSS2DObject/HTML sprites so hbar and subscripts render crisply; keep them screen-space constant size. On lValue change, rebuild the vector set and arc radius with a short tween so the learner sees the arc grow and new vectors appear. Highlighting for mState: dim non-selected vectors to 20% opacity and grey, keep the selected one full olive with its dashed projection line and tick label emphasized; 'all' restores everything. Toggle to 'Classical continuum' fades in the grey ray fan behind the green vectors without removing them.  Hover picking via raycast against invisible thicker cylinder proxies along each vector.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button / state for allowed m values: the learner steps through m = -3 to 3, one green L vector highlights at a time and its dashed projection lands on the matching hbar tick, showing that the z component is quantized while the vector length stays fixed.

authoredContext:
The quantization of the polar angle for the l=3 state is shown in the figure. The orbital angular momentum vector lies somewhere on the surface of a cone with an opening angle θ relative to the z-axis (unless m=0, in which case θ=90° and the vector points are perpendicular to the z-axis).

The quantization of orbital angular momentum. Each vector lies on the surface of a cone with axis along the z-axis.

Seven vector, all of the same length L, are drawn at 7 different angles to the z axis. The z components of the vectors are indicated both by horizontal lines from the tip of the vector to the z axis and by labels on the z axis. For four of the vectors, the angle between the z axis and the vector is also labeled. The z component values are 3 h bar at angle theta sub three, 2 h bar at angle theta sub two, h bar at angle theta sub one, zero at angle theta sub zero, minus h bar, minus 2 h bar, and minus 3 h bar.

A detailed study of angular momentum reveals that we cannot know all three components simultaneously. In the previous section, the z-component of orbital angular momentum has definite values that depend on the quantum number m. This implies that we cannot know both x- and y-components of angular momentum, Lx and Ly, with certainty. As a result, the precise direction of the orbital angular momentum vector is unknown.

discrepancies: The θ₀–θ₃ arc labels are crowded near the origin and render smaller/tighter than in the source, where the angle labels are well separated and comfortably readable along the z axis side.
The L⃗ vector label renders as a small 'L' with a faint overbar-like arrow rather than the prominent bold L with vector arrow shown at the top right of the source.
Arrowheads terminate slightly inside the dashed magnitude arc, whereas in the source the tips sit essentially on the arc.

Horizontal axis extends only slightly to the left of the origin and stops before the arc's right edge; in the source it extends symmetrically well past the origin on the left and beyond the arc on the right.
evaluation.notes: A near-exact reproduction of the space-quantization fan with correct vector count, dashed arc, ħ-step projection lines and θ arcs, backed by a rich and pedagogically sound set of interactions (m isolation, l slider, classical continuum, guided demo); only minor label sizing/crowding and a weak L⃗ glyph detract.
action_items: Increase θ₀–θ₃ label font size and push them further along their arc radii so they don't crowd near the origin, matching the source's clear spacing.
Render the L⃗ label larger/bold with a proper vector arrow (e.g. styled overset arrow) so it reads like the source annotation.
Extend the arrow lengths (or shorten the head offset) so the tips land exactly on the dashed magnitude arc, and extend the horizontal axis a bit further left and right to match the source framing.

Colors: vectors and arrowheads olive green #84A625 (line width ~3px, solid triangular heads); axes, arc, projection lines, angle arcs, tick labels all black/dark grey #1A1A1A, with the arc and projection lines dashed (~6px dash, 4px gap); classical-continuum fan drawn in grey #BBBBBB at 35% opacity with ~60 evenly spaced thin rays over 0–180°.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera looking down -Z at the xz-plane (pure 2D). Build arrows from THREE.Line/shaft + ConeGeometry or a Line2 with a small triangle mesh head so head size stays constant. Dashed elements via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Labels (z, 3ħ…-3ħ, θ0–θ3, vector L) as CSS2DObject/HTML sprites so hbar and subscripts render crisply; keep them screen-space constant size. On lValue change, rebuild the vector set and arc radius with a short tween so the learner sees the arc grow and new vectors appear. Highlighting for mState: dim non-selected vectors to 20% opacity and grey, keep the selected one full olive with its dashed projection line and tick label emphasized; 'all' restores everything. Toggle to 'Classical continuum' fades in the grey ray fan behind the green vectors without removing them.  Hover picking via raycast against invisible thicker cylinder proxies along each vector.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure is a two-dimensional vector diagram of the allowed orientations of an orbital angular momentum vector. A vertical axis labeled z rises from an origin set at the left of the frame and is crossed there by an unlabeled horizontal axis. Seven olive-green arrows of identical length fan out from the origin into the right half of the plane, their tips landing on a dashed circular arc that makes their common magnitude explicit; the topmost arrow is labeled L with a vector arrow. A dashed horizontal line runs from each tip back to the z axis, which is ticked and labeled from top to bottom 3ħ, 2ħ, ħ, then the unlabeled origin, then -ħ, -2ħ, and -3ħ, so the arrows step in equal increments of z component rather than in equal angles. Four thin arcs of increasing radius sweep from the positive z axis to the four upper arrows and are labeled θ0 nearest the origin, then θ1, θ2, and θ3; the θ0 arc opens all the way to the horizontal arrow while the θ3 arc closes on the steepest one. Holding the arrow length fixed while stepping the projections in equal units shows that only a discrete set of polar angles is available to the vector.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button / state for allowed m values: the learner steps through m = -3 to 3, one green L vector highlights at a time and its dashed projection lands on the matching hbar tick, showing that the z component is quantized while the vector length stays fixed.
- Toggle between discrete and continuous angles: the learner switches from the seven allowed vectors to a faint continuous fan, making clear that the diagram permits only selected polar angles rather than any orientation.
- Slider for quantum number l: the learner changes l, the number of allowed projection states and the common vector length update together, revealing how angular-momentum magnitude and allowed Lz values are linked.

discrepancies: θ0–θ3 labels are pushed outward along the arc bisectors so they sit on top of / right next to the green vectors, whereas in the source they sit clearly in the open wedge to the left of the vectors near the z axis — this reduces readability and makes it ambiguous which arc each label belongs to.

Angle arcs in the source start at the z axis and are noticeably longer/wider (they extend well to the right past the labels); the generated arcs are shorter and more tightly nested, making the θ annotation region look more cramped than the original.
The generated figure adds an origin sphere and a longer leftward extension of the horizontal axis; the source has a plain crossing of the two axes with no dot (minor cosmetic addition).
Tick marks/labels (3ħ, 2ħ, ħ …) are rendered at a smaller relative size than in the source, where the ħ annotations are prominent, so the figure reads slightly 'thinner' than the original.

The vector for m = 0 in the source terminates with its arrowhead on the dashed arc on the horizontal axis with no projection line; the generated version matches, but the dashed arc endpoints (25°–155°) are cut shorter than the source arc, which visually spans nearly the full ±3ħ tips.
